body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw full-donor \(\widehat\tau\). This equality is identified under event transport. Exact finite-sample conditional coverage and the asymptotic upper risk and expected-length bounds hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) for every nonempty compatible envelope. The matched four-channel lower frontier holds for fixed \(B>(Sd)^2\), with constants permitted to depend on the fixed slack; at \(B=(Sd)^2\), only the treated, smoothing, and spacing lower channels are asserted. Configurations \(B<(Sd)^2\) are empty. Historical response laws may be heterogeneous across units subject to boundedness and a common conditional mean; geometric beta mixing is imposed only on the design process. The donor component remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus, and no sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering condition is imposed.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero. Only the stacked historical design process is geometrically beta mixing. This allows logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels. Unit response laws may be heterogeneous across and within cohorts, provided their historical conditional mean is the common \(m_s\); each unit's entire calendar response path is otherwise an unrestricted cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and a standardized fourth-moment envelope; historical training coordinates are exact. Writing \(D=Sd\), nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\), and the donor lower experiment uses fixed strict slack \(B>D^2\); the estimator and interval do not. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions for financial event-study estimators and explains that buy-and-hold comparisons require volatility matching.
The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.
The many-period--many-control result gives conditions for synthetic-control factor-loading recovery under imperfect pre-treatment fit.
The proximal synthetic-control theorems identify treatment effects by using excluded control outcomes as predetermined proxies.

body.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw local-polynomial estimator is exactly a cohort-weighted event coefficient. Over the full-design-centered class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), bounded unit response laws may be heterogeneous subject only to a common conditional mean, while geometric beta mixing is imposed on the historical design process alone. Nonemptiness forces the joint wealth and donor fourth-moment envelope to satisfy \(B\ge(Sd)^2\). For fixed interior-compatible \(B>(Sd)^2\), matching bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\); at \(B=(Sd)^2\), the upper bounds and exact finite-sample conditional coverage remain valid, but only the treated, smoothing, and spacing lower channels are claimed. The feasible construction projects the full independent donor mean once, uses one normalized-shape local-polynomial fit per cohort, and combines bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding radii with exact Holder--Taylor and donor-modulus allowances. The log-adjusted spacing term is unavoidable uniformly, and under strict envelope slack the donor channel saturates at \(N^{-1}\) in mean squared error when \(\lambda>1\), conditional on the two-sided local modulus.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory mainly treats linear return contrasts; repeated-measurement regression fixes the query; generated-regressor theory typically moves training coordinates; and synthetic-control inference does not deliver a generated-event-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth under arbitrary relative growth.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture here observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, and generated-center uncertainty without a classical measurement-error inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact cohortwise weighted-panel coefficient representation, exact finite-sample conditional coverage over every nonempty compatible envelope, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers when the standardized donor fourth-moment envelope has fixed strict slack above \((Sd)^2\). At the equality boundary it retains the same feasible upper bounds and the treated, smoothing, and spacing converses without asserting a universal donor converse. A normalized Gram-shape selector under design-only geometric beta mixing, full-data bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding calibration, an exact Taylor allowance, full-sample covariance-standardized donor control, and channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish these results without donor splitting, sequential overlap, a dense-site condition, an upper local-mass condition, or identical unit response laws.

body.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching; their work informs the event-transport layer rather than supplying this frontier. Barber and Lyon (1997), Mitchell and Stafford (2000), and Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the warning that matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth. That warning is motivation, not a theorem here and not an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation, Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution, and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study local-polynomial regression evaluated at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer. Those experiments differ from the exact historical coordinates and single generated event query here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block-coupling template; here dependence is imposed only on the historical design. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for arbitrary relative growth, and Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies without deriving the generated-proxy minimax frontier. The present proof adds one full-donor center, heterogeneous bounded unit-response clusters with a common conditional mean, exact finite-sample conditional coverage, an explicit rare-block spacing witness, and the necessary distinction between strict and boundary donor-moment compatibility.
body.interpretation: For every integer \(T\ge3\), the replicated-smoothing term obeys \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), where \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\). Hence the active upper risk is exactly \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\): smoothing remains useful bookkeeping but is never uniquely active. For fixed interior-compatible \(B>(Sd)^2\), this is also the matched lower frontier: the oracle region has \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})\), the generated-proxy region reverses that relation, and the boundary equates the two. The sole donor elbow is \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). At the compatible moment boundary \(B=(Sd)^2\), the same upper diagram holds but no universal donor converse is claimed, so the generated-proxy phase is not declared minimax-sharp there. The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball or anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The risk and honest-length results additionally use the two explicit full-design mean-stability and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence. Geometric beta mixing is required only for the historical design, and bounded unit response paths may otherwise be arbitrarily dependent over time and heterogeneous across units subject to their common conditional mean. Nonemptiness forces \(B\ge(Sd)^2\); the four-channel lower frontier additionally requires fixed strict slack \(B>(Sd)^2\), while exact coverage and upper bounds do not. At equality only the three non-donor lower channels are asserted. The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass. The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp minimax constants.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification, the exact full-donor FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, a log-adjusted selector bound under design-only geometric beta mixing, a positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, compatible causal-panel lower-bound embeddings, a matching conditional-risk and expected-length frontier for fixed \(B>(Sd)^2\), and an exact finite-sample conditionally honest interval over every nonempty compatible envelope. At \(B=(Sd)^2\), the estimator, exact coverage, and upper bounds remain proved, together with treated, smoothing, and spacing lower bounds, but no universal donor converse. Historical and event unit response laws may be heterogeneous and each unit's calendar history is treated as one bounded cluster. No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, or temporal-outcome mixing condition is used. The donor converse remains conditional on both strict envelope slack and the two-sided local modulus, and causal interpretation remains conditional on event transport.
